processes.name: Sitara deal price/volume corrections and missing-deal chasers
processes.description: Schedulers and settlements analysts email Daren Farmer's logistics group when Sitara deals have wrong prices or volumes, or when a counterparty invoices a deal that cannot be found. Each case is a thread of manual lookups, spreadsheet re-sends and 'let me know when changed' follow-ups.
processes.stall_points: Requester must wait for someone else to edit Sitara and then notify back; volumes spreadsheet is re-sent; root cause (who added a meter or deal) needs multi-party digging across companies.
processes.automation: A deal-correction request form feeding a tracked ticket with deal number, field, old and new value, and automatic notification on completion; a deal-audit lookup that shows who changed a ticket and when.

evidence.quote: Deal 895691 - swing deal - currently has 234,000 in the scheduled column and it should be 441,000 based on the spreadsheet I sent.

Conoco is saying that we did not buy that gas from them.
ENA was invoiced by Coral Energy for two deals on Tejas for June 2001 that I do not see in the system.

processes.name: Late pathing, bridgeback errors and transport ticket requests
processes.description: Volume management and logistics staff ask schedulers to path deals, create transport usage tickets or fix late-pathed deals so pool balances and bridgeback to Sitara clear. Requests are forwarded and re-forwarded until the owner acts.
processes.stall_points: Requests sit with the owner for weeks and are re-sent as chasers; the original email has to be forwarded again to the person who needs it.
processes.automation: A shared exception queue of unbalanced pools and bridgeback errors with owner, age and automatic reminders instead of forwarded emails.

evidence.quote: This deal expired 12/31/00, and the late pathing has caused a bridgeback error for January and February 2001.

processes.name: West hourly desk EOL deal entry and book allocation rules
processes.description: The short-term West hourly desk enters EOL trades in Enpower/CAPS under rules the manager keeps restating by group email (which book, one deal per strip, inter-desk deals by night shift, INC sheets). Unmatched broker deals are also chased by back office.
processes.stall_points: The same entry rules are re-explained in several emails because volumes outgrew the process; deals go missing in Enpower and back office finds mismatches weeks later.
processes.automation: Auto-create EOL deals in Enpower with book and strip defaults and run a daily match of broker deals to Enpower to flag gaps.

evidence.quote: A standardization in our process will benefit the entire group and will allow us to make consistent improvements as time goes on.
INC SHEETS MUST BE MAINTAINED, DEALS ENTERED AND ROUTED EACH HOUR--only way to stay ahead
The night shift will average the sales price and make one strip for the on-peak piece.

processes.name: Counterparty dispute and settlement reconciliation (tapes, imbalance, profit splits)
processes.description: Disputes with El Paso Electric, SRP and MPC are resolved by requesting trade tapes, listening, and drafting emails to counterparties, with the manager reviewing wording. Back-office staff also ask the manager to explain or decide historic deal splits and annuities.
processes.stall_points: Tape access is limited and requests go through another person; disputes drag for months (five months on MPC March) and need the manager to make the call.
processes.automation: A dispute tracker linking each disputed deal to its tape request, evidence and decision, with templated counterparty emails.

evidence.quote: In an effort to curb El Paso settlements issues, I've requested several sets of tapes over the past few days.

processes.name: Short/long position notices to the scheduling shift
processes.description: The desk manager or scheduler emails the shift analyst the megawatts, hours, price and counterparties for a short or long position, with notes to check price with other traders. Each notice is typed by hand.
processes.stall_points: Details such as price and counterparty are deferred to 'check with' other people; shift staff must interpret free-text emails and re-key into deal systems.
processes.automation: A structured position-change form that writes directly into the deal sheet and notifies the shift.

processes.name: Standing trading-procedure reminders to the real-time group
processes.description: The desk manager repeatedly emails the whole group procedure reminders (tiered bids, congestion bidding, generation waivers, weekend California scheduling, congestion allocation). Each is a manual broadcast.
processes.stall_points: Rules live in emails, so new staff make the same errors and the manager re-sends reminders; wrong tiered bids cost real money.
processes.automation: A single maintained procedure page with checks (for example tier-bid validation) rather than repeated broadcast emails.

evidence.quote: we must begin adjust bidding for congestion at ALL tie points.

processes.name: Month-end close and ISO revenue true-up
processes.description: Month-end involves a published close schedule with a no-changes cutoff, collection of reports and exception notes from schedulers, and a reconciliation of daily ISO revenue/expenses against volume management totals.
processes.stall_points: Schedulers were confused about when changes were allowed; true-up covered only July variances while August variances were unaccounted and needed manual follow-up.
processes.automation: Automated cutoff reminders and a variance report comparing daily ISO flash to month-end totals.

evidence.quote: At 6PM Friday (or before if you are ready) I will be by to pick up the reports and exceptions dialogue.

processes.name: IT, telecom and equipment requests and chasers
processes.description: Staff request desktops, turrets, phones and cellular plan changes through email or an automatic notification system, and then chase status and supply details.
processes.stall_points: Delivery gets rescheduled and the requester must chase and answer follow-up questions by email.
processes.automation: A request portal with status tracking and pre-collected setup details.
